title: City people named as directors on contract notices that the organization’s own return contradicts
question: Where a contractor’s notice names a City employee or official as a director, does the organization’s tax return agree, and how old are the lists contractors file?
finding: 44 City people named as directors on notices while in City service where the organization’s return says otherwise: 21 named after the return says the seat ended, 23 never listed on a return for those years. More widely, 265 director names at 74 organizations stay on 720 notices dated more than a year after the organization’s return shows them gone (most: Chinatown Community Development Center, 25 names, latest notice 2026-09-25).
how: For funded organizations with tax returns on disk, each name listed as “Board of Directors” on a notice was compared with Part VII of the returns: the last year the name is listed, a term end written into the title, and whether any later return omits it. The upper rows are the names that also belong to a City employee or Form 700 filer in service on the notice date.
limits: The likeliest reading is that the source is wrong, not the conduct: contractors and departments reuse an old board list when a notice is filed. That matters because the notice is the list of people barred from giving to the approving official, and because it can show a City official on a grantee’s board after the seat was given up, or hide who sits there now. Returns can be the stale record instead, and nicknames or changed surnames make a name look absent.
